justification: The homepage hero is the primary entry point and the reports hub routes every satellite tool; a regression here silently strands visitors on a hub with no address carried through, so it warrants defensive tests and three-state param handling, though it touches no database and no regulatory data.

pre_impl.existing_data: The hero box was a TrackedLink dressed as an input; grepped for existing hero-search islands and found only HomeHero which routes to /property in a light theme and the reports LandingHero card, neither routing to the hub with the address, so a thin client wrapper over the shared AddressAutocomplete primitive was the right reuse.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: Confirmed each report tool page already reads params.address, flood checks hasAddress and granny-flat already links to itself with an encoded address, so carrying the address into the hub genuinely pre-fills and auto-runs the chosen tool rather than being purely cosmetic.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: New client island reuses AddressAutocomplete and trackFunnelCta; the reports hub becomes an async server component reading searchParams; no new data source, no backend call, and no database schema is touched by this change.

functions.name: HeroAddressSearch
functions.input: no props; local state holds the typed NSW address string entered in the input
functions.output: renders a real address input that pushes /reports with the encoded address on submit or suggestion select
functions.if_none: an empty or whitespace-only address short-circuits inside go so no navigation and no funnel event fire

functions.name: ReportsLanding
functions.input: awaited searchParams whose optional address key arrives from the homepage hero search box
functions.output: tool grid whose card hrefs carry the encoded address plus an active-address banner when an address is present
functions.if_none: a missing or non-string address yields an empty suffix so the hub renders bare tool links and hides the banner

values.read_at: ReportsLanding server component awaits searchParams then narrows the optional address key
values.if_missing: the typeof guard treats undefined or an array param as no address, so the hub falls back to plain tool links

break_it.scenario: A visitor pastes an address containing commas and spaces then clicks a tool card expecting that exact property to load
break_it.what_happens: an unencoded address would break the query string so the downstream tool geocodes a truncated or empty value
break_it.how: the address is passed through encodeURIComponent in both the hero push and the hub href suffix, so commas and spaces survive as escape sequences
break_it.repro: type 14 Hunter St, Lewisham NSW in the hero, submit, then click Flood Risk Check and inspect the resulting reports flood address URL

break_it.scenario: A crafted link supplies the address key twice so searchParams.address arrives as an array instead of a plain string
break_it.what_happens: serialising that array into the href would emit a comma-joined value and mislead every downstream tool page
break_it.how: ReportsLanding only accepts a string via typeof narrowing so an array falls through to the empty suffix and the plain hub renders
break_it.repro: open the reports hub with the address supplied twice and confirm the tool card hrefs contain no address query at all

break_it.scenario: The Google Maps Places script has not finished initialising when a visitor starts typing into the hero address box
break_it.what_happens: with no autocomplete dropdown a link-only box would leave the visitor stuck, which is exactly the fake-input bug being fixed
break_it.how: the box is a genuine text field inside a form with a submit arrow, so typing and pressing the arrow routes even when no suggestion list has appeared
break_it.repro: block maps.googleapis.com in the browser, type an address into the hero, and confirm the arrow button still navigates to the reports hub

post_merge.manual_verify: Reproduced the original bug on the preview where clicking the homepage hero box navigated to the reports hub with no address; after the fix tsc is clean and six new jest tests plus the full frontend suite pass, with a final visual check on the Vercel preview once this branch deploys.
